question: Which foundries does NVIDIA say produce its semiconductor wafers in its fiscal 2026 10-K?
reference_answer: NVIDIA uses foundries such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and Samsung Electronics to produce its semiconductor wafers (NVDA 10-K, page 10).

question: What are AMD's three reportable segments in its fiscal 2025 10-K?
reference_answer: Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded (AMD 10-K, page 8).

question: What are Micron's four business units in its fiscal 2026 10-K?
reference_answer: Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU), Core Data Center Business Unit (CDBU), Mobile and Client Business Unit (MCBU), and Automotive and Embedded Business Unit (AEBU) (MU 10-K, page 143).

question: What four components does Intel list as its foundry offerings in its fiscal 2025 10-K?
reference_answer: Wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, chiplet integration, and design enablement services (INTC 10-K, page 11).

question: What two industry firsts does Intel say the Intel 18A process introduces in its fiscal 2025 10-K?
reference_answer: Gate-all-around transistors (RibbonFET) and backside power delivery (PowerVia) (INTC 10-K, page 9).

question: How many employees did NVIDIA (end of fiscal 2026) and AMD (end of fiscal 2025) report?
reference_answer: NVIDIA: approximately 42,000 employees in 38 countries (NVDA 10-K, page 15). AMD: approximately 31,000 employees as of December 27 2025 (AMD 10-K, page 19).

question: NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 10-K names its memory suppliers. Is Micron one of them and which Micron business unit sells HBM according to Micron's fiscal 2026 10-K?
reference_answer: Yes. NVIDIA buys memory from SK Hynix, Micron Technology and Samsung (NVDA 10-K, page 10). Micron's Cloud Memory Business Unit (CMBU) covers HBM for all data center customers (MU 10-K, pages 13 and 143).
